questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official match records, corroborated by contemporaneous match reports, for the September 2026 Manchester derby hosted by Manchester United. Resolution : Resolve to the club with more goals in the official final score after the match, including stoppage time. If the scores are level, resolve to “Draw”. Accepted Answer Format : The winning club's name, or “Draw” if neither club wins.
questions.current_reasoning: Upgrading Manchester City (0.40 -> 0.47) and downgrading Manchester United (0.34 -> 0.28) following contrasting Aug 28-29 match and injury updates. On Friday Aug 28, Enzo Maresca's City routed Crystal Palace 4-1 away via braces from Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki to sit top of the Premier League with 6 points from two games, with €100m midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi ready and Enzo Fernandez's permanent move from Chelsea resolved Aug 27. Conversely, entering United's Aug 30 match against Ipswich Town after their toothless 2-0 opening loss at Hull City, Michael Carrick confirmed on Aug 29 that £70m signing Carlos Baleba is ruled out for ~3 weeks with an ankle injury—jeopardizing his participation in the Sep 13 derby—while Manuel Ugarte faces a long-term knee ligament tear and Matthijs de Ligt, Amad Diallo, and Mason Mount are also currently sidelined. Even accounting for Old Trafford home advantage and United's attacking core (PFA Player of the Year Bruno Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha, Mbeumo), City's sharper early form and United's defensive/midfield injuries shift Dixon-Coles expected goals to ~1.70 vs ~1.27 (47% City, 28% United, 25% Draw).

local_articles.title: England eyes series win after Pakistan slumps to 53-3 in a 389 chase at Lord’s
local_articles.snippet: LONDON: England was eyeing a series win after reducing Pakistan to 53-3 in a chase of 389 on the fourth morning of the second test at Lord’s on Sunday. Ollie Robinson dismissed Azan Awais and Abdullah Shafique and Jofra Archer bounced out captain Babar Azam in the first eight overs. Saud Shakeel, 23 off 36 balls, and opener Shan Masood, 15 off 42, hung on to lunch. Under partial sunshine, Pakistan finished England’s second innings at 208 before noon but the host had a mountainous lead of 388 runs. That had to be daunting for a Pakistan side that hasn’t cracked 200 in three previous innings in the series. The first at Lord’s was only 110 on Friday, and two days later England’s all-seam attack was ruthlessly picking apart the top order again. questions.title: Which film will win the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Venice Film Festival?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Venice Film Festival’s official announcement of its 2026 award winners. Resolution : Resolve to the film awarded the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 festival, once the winner is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning film’s title.
questions.current_reasoning: Breaking Aug 24 announcement: Venice Film Festival organizers added 'NAZA' as a late 21st title in the main Golden Lion competition—the sole documentary in the lineup. Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor (co-directors of Oscar-winning 'No Other Land') and produced/executive-produced by James Wilson and Jonathan Glazer (the exact team behind 'The Zone of Interest' and last year's Venice Grand Jury Prize runner-up 'The Voice of Hind Rajab'), 'NAZA' premieres late in the festival on Sept 10 before a jury chaired by Maggie Gyllenhaal that also includes 'Hind Rajab' director Kaouther Ben Hania, Johnnie To, and Daniel Blumberg. Because documentaries are rarely awarded Best Director, Screenplay, or Acting prizes, strong jury support concentrates directly on Golden Lion, Grand Jury Prize, and especially the Special Jury Prize (matching Venice's track record for urgent political works like 'Green Border'), vaulting 'NAZA' to #1 at 0.09 (replacing 'The Echo Chamber' in top 5). With the competition expanded to 21 films (uniform baseline 0.048) and no premieres until Sept 2, we trim Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love' (0.08 -> 0.07) and Werner Herzog's 'Bucking Fastard' (0.07 -> 0.06) while holding Hirokazu Kore-eda's 'Look Back' (0.07) and May el-Toukhy's 'Woman Unknown' (0.07), leaving 64% across the remaining 16 titles until screenings and reviews begin.
